    Two-observation orphanhood estimates using the Timaeus coefficients

    orphanhood_two_timaeus.Rd

    Internal worker for the Timaeus two-census orphanhood variant used by orphanhood_two(). It converts changes in the proportion not orphaned into conditional parental survival and then into interpolated life-table survivorship.

    orphanhood_two_timaeus(
  prop1_not_orphan,
  prop2_not_orphan,
  age,
  date1,
  date2,
  maternal,
  mac1,
  mac2,
  mlt_data_input,
  mlt_family,
  brass_logit,
  brass_logit_e0,
  HIV_prev,
  HIV_art,
  HIV_5q0,
  sex,
  y,
  z,
  timaes_coeff,
  e0_accept,
  verbose
)

    Arguments

    prop1_not_orphan, prop2_not_orphan

    Numeric vectors with proportions of respondents with a surviving parent in the first and second observations.

    age

    Integer vector with lower bounds of respondent age groups common to both observations.

    date1, date2

    Numeric decimal years for the first and second observations.

    maternal

    Logical. TRUE for maternal orphanhood, FALSE for paternal orphanhood.

    mac1, mac2

    Numeric mean ages at childbearing in the first and second observations.

    mlt_data_input

    Optional user-supplied model life table. Use with brass_logit = TRUE.

    mlt_family

    Character vector of model life table families.

    brass_logit

    Logical. If TRUE, apply one-parameter Brass logit smoothing against the selected or supplied standard.

    brass_logit_e0

    Numeric life expectancy at birth used when brass_logit = TRUE.

    HIV_prev, HIV_art, HIV_5q0

    Optional HIV prevalence, ART coverage, and child mortality inputs for the HIV variant.

    sex

    Character. "f" for female mortality or "m" for male mortality.

    y, z

    Numeric parental exact-age anchors used in the Timaeus conversion.

    timaes_coeff

    Data frame of Timaeus coefficients for the selected maternal or paternal variant.

    e0_accept

    Numeric vector of length 2 with acceptable implied e0 range.

    verbose

    Logical. If TRUE, print diagnostic messages.

    Value

    A list with lx_estimates.

    Examples

    # \donttest{
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

standard_iusssp <- data.frame(
  age = seq(15, 85, 5),
  lx = c(
    0.8868, 0.8763, 0.8621, 0.8467, 0.8296,
    0.8094, 0.7845, 0.7527, 0.7096, 0.6515,
    0.5724, 0.4700, 0.3443, 0.2101, 0.0962
  )
)
paternal_coeff <- data.frame(
  age = c(25, 30, 35, 40),
  a = c(-0.0554, -0.7539, -1.0809, -1.1726),
  b = c(0.00757, 0.01558, 0.02273, 0.02647),
  c = c(0.0239, 0.6452, 0.9289, 0.9381),
  d = c(0.8080, 0.6498, 0.4807, 0.4372)
)

salomons_1986_1999_paternal <- MortIndEst:::orphanhood_two_timaeus(
  prop1_not_orphan = c(
    0.9644, 0.9340, 0.8862, 0.8088,
    0.7060, 0.5812, 0.4620, 0.3317
  ),
  prop2_not_orphan = c(
    0.9710, 0.9454, 0.9071, 0.8493,
    0.7717, 0.6568, 0.5375, 0.3891
  ),
  age = seq(5, 40, 5),
  date1 = 1986.9,
  date2 = 1999.9,
  maternal = FALSE,
  mac1 = 34.08,
  mac2 = 34.08,
  mlt_data_input = standard_iusssp,
  mlt_family = "CD_West",
  brass_logit = TRUE,
  brass_logit_e0 = 60,
  HIV_prev = NULL,
  HIV_art = NULL,
  HIV_5q0 = NULL,
  sex = "m",
  y = 35,
  z = 55,
  timaes_coeff = paternal_coeff,
  e0_accept = c(20, 100),
  verbose = FALSE
)
head(salomons_1986_1999_paternal$lx_estimates)
#>   age prop1_not_orphan prop2_not_orphan  mac1  mac2 type      alpha age_mlt
